column1: # confusables.tsv - character folding table for phishing lookalike detection.
#   Primary reference: Unicode Standard Annex #39 (UTS #39), "Unicode Security Mechanisms",
#   HONESTY NOTE - this is a hand-curated TRANSCRIPTION of the high-value subset, not a
#   verified machine extract. Phase 1 runs offline, so confusables.txt was not fetched and
#   diffed against these rows. Each row states the code point it claims to map, so the table
#   can be audited row by row against the published file. The codepoint is the
#   authoritative disambiguator; the UTS #39 name in the note is descriptive.
#   Rows not drawn from UTS #39 are marked `leet` in the script column and are listed as
#   such in the header below. Nothing here is a bulk import: an unreviewed 6k-entry table
#   would be an unaccountable input to a lookalike score.
#   Why not embed the full file: zero third-party dependencies (ARCHITECTURE.md L215), and a
#   curated set stays reviewable. A missing mapping degrades detection recall slightly; it
#   cannot corrupt a score, because every folded character still passes through the same
# NON-UTS ROWS (leetspeak digit/letter substitution, standard in phishing domains)
#   These exist so that "paypa1.com" and "paypal.com" reduce to one skeleton. Skeletons are
#   used only for lookalike *distance* and registry *equivalence*, never for display or for
#   any address that is sent to, clicked, or replied to.
# FORMAT (tab-separated; no tab characters inside any field)
#   col 1  source  - one code point, or the literal text "U+XXXX"
#   col 2  target  - the ASCII replacement; may be more than one character
#                    ("bl" for Cyrillic yery, as in UTS #39)
#   col 3  script  - origin script of the source, drives the mixed_script rule
# INVARIANTS - both enforced at load time by TextNormalizer.loadMap()
#   1. normalise() is IDEMPOTENT: folding the target string must return it unchanged.
#      TextNormalizer.verifyIdempotent() checks this for every row and refuses to load a
#      table that violates it. This is what keeps the domain registry's add-then-compare
#   2. No two rows may map the same source to different targets. A conflict is a load error,
#      not a last-one-wins overwrite, because a silently shadowed row is an unlogged input.
# Lines beginning with '#' and blank lines are ignored.

column1: # NOTE: U+0437 CYRILLIC SMALL LETTER ZE looks like the digit 3, which UTS #39 does map. It is
# DELIBERATELY ABSENT here. Folding it to '3' collides with the leet row 3->e, so the fold
# would chain ZE -> 3 -> e and the result would no longer resemble the input. Dropping the row
# costs a little recall on a character attackers do not actually use; keeping it would produce
# a wrong skeleton. The load-time idempotence check in TextNormalizer rejects such a row, which
# U+0417 CYRILLIC CAPITAL LETTER ZE omitted for the same reason as U+0437 above: 3 -> e chains.
# --- Cyrillic singletons and mixed-case letters. UTS #39 -----------------
# U+04CF CYRILLIC SMALL LETTER PALOCHKA omitted: UTS #39 maps it to the digit 1, which collides
# with the leet row 1 -> l. Same chaining hazard as the ZE rows.

# --- UTS #39 rows added to close probe-found gaps (2026-09-29) --------------
# The rows above are a hand transcription. A regression probe that feeds a fully Greek
# spelling of paypal" (pi-alpha-upsilon-pi-alpha-lambda) exposed a real detection gap:

column1: # GREEK PI and GREEK LAMDA were absent, so the word reduced to a skeleton still full of
# Greek characters and lookalike_strong never fired. Transliterating only SOME Greek letters
# (alpha, rho, upsilon) while omitting pi and lambda produced a confidently WRONG skeleton,
# which is worse than no folding at all.
# TONE ACCENTS are included deliberately. A phisher using Greek keyboard layout produces
# accented forms (upsilon with tonos) far more often than the bare letters, and a table that
# handles bare upsilon but not accented upsilon fails on exactly the traffic it is meant to
# catch. GREEK THETA is deliberately NOT mapped: it resembles "0", and 0 is itself a source
# row mapping to "o", so theta->0->o would break the load-time idempotence invariant.

column4: GREEK CAPITAL LETTER ALPHA WITH TONOS
GREEK SMALL LETTER ALPHA WITH OXIA
GREEK SMALL LETTER ALPHA WITH TONOS
GREEK SMALL LETTER IOTA WITH TONOS
GREEK SMALL LETTER OMICRON WITH TONOS
GREEK SMALL LETTER UPSILON WITH TONOS; see U+03C5 note on the y/u choice
GREEK SMALL LETTER OMEGA WITH TONOS

column1: # DEAD ROWS DELIBERATELY NOT ADDED, despite appearing in UTS #39's confusables data:
#   U+03D5 GREEK PHI SYMBOL, U+03D6 GREEK PI SYMBOL, U+03F2 GREEK UPSILON WITH HOOK,
#   U+03F9 GREEK CAPITAL LUNATE SIGMA SYMBOL, U+FF62/U+FF63 HALFWIDTH CORNER BRACKETS
# These are CANONICALLY or COMPATIBILITY EQUIVALENT to other code points. TextNormalizer
# applies NFKC before consulting this table, so normalise() never sees the symbol form at
# all - it is already rewritten to the other code point, which is mapped here. Adding rows
# for them would be unreachable configuration: they would appear in mappingCount(), look
# load-bearing in review, and never execute. This was found by a probe that compared every
# row on disk against what normalise() actually does, and it is why the U+FF62/U+FF63 rows
# were repointed at U+300C/U+300D: the old rows were dead AND their intended effect
# (mapping bracket variants to a quote) was silently not happening.
# --- Cyrillic rows added to close probe-found gaps (2026-09-29) -------------
# EF and IO-WITH-DIAERESIS render as o/e to a Latin reader and were missing. They are the
# reason "poypal" style substitutions were silently undetected in single-character probes.

column4: CYRILLIC CAPITAL LETTER IO WITH DIAERESIS
CYRILLIC SMALL LETTER IO WITH DIAERESIS
